races.name: hamilton-park.co.uk Amateur Jockeys' Handicap

runners_data.name: Zu Run
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse returning to 6f for first time since December but showed good form over 7f at Brighton recently
runners_data.comment: C&D winner last May but only pieces of form since; cheekpieces return off career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Three 7f wins; this is his first 6f run since December 2024 but he arrives after a good second at Brighton (good to firm) and holds each-way claims.

runners_data.name: Mister Sky Blue
runners_data.note: Course and distance winner with solid recent form, typical hold-up style suits if pace collapses
runners_data.comment: Kept on well for second here 19 days ago after a break; thereabouts
runners_data.spotlight: C&D win last May (good to firm) remains his only win from 20 starts; he has run two solid races in defeat this year, however, and would seem highly likely to run his race once more.

runners_data.name: Endowed
runners_data.note: Class horse returning after 252-day break, won twice at 6f last year but freshness concern
runners_data.spotlight: Won two 6f handicaps at Chepstow last June and went close in his hat-trick bid in July (7f); two lesser efforts followed and he returns to action after 252 days on the sidelines.

runners_data.name: No Nay Nevermind
runners_data.note: Only prominent runner in field of hold-up horses, crucial tactical advantage despite poor recent form
runners_data.comment: Twice runner-up off a higher mark at Newcastle late last year, but now 0-18
runners_data.spotlight: 0-19; runner-up twice in 7f AW handicaps in late 2025 but this year's efforts leave her with a point to prove.

runners_data.name: Penny Mountain
runners_data.note: Hold-up style but recent 6f AW win suggests she can adapt to faster pace if needed
runners_data.comment: Fifth at Musselburgh latest and that form has taken a few knocks since; 1m questionable.
runners_data.spotlight: 6f AW win on New Year's Day; several good runs in defeat have followed and dropping back to 6f could prove beneficial.

runners_data.name: Shoptilyoudrop
runners_data.note: Exposed maiden returning after 124-day break, easily dismissed on form
runners_data.comment: Little to shout about for some time and now 0-20; best to look elsewhere
runners_data.spotlight: Exposed 21-race maiden; ran one of her better races when fourth at Wolverhampton in February when last seen but still easy enough to swerve.

runners_data.name: Doon The Glen
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse with two seconds this year, visor back on after good recent course form
runners_data.comment: Only 1-32 and vast majority of his form is at sprint distances; likely to get outstayed
runners_data.spotlight: Just one win from 33 starts but he has twice finished second this year (both 6f, AW and good to firm); return to sprinting can help, as should the return of a visor, and he helps form a strong hand for Jim Goldie.

runners_data.name: Summerstorms Dream
runners_data.note: Slow starter with cheekpieces added, needs to overcome early positioning issues
runners_data.comment: Doing best work late when 3rd over C&D (12-1) fortnight ago; one of three for Jim Goldie.
runners_data.spotlight: Slow starts have been a recurring theme since she moved into handicaps but she has hinted that her mark is in range; cheekpieces added and Eireann Cagney is booked, so there can be encouragement for an improved showing tonight.

runners_data.name: Pebble Dash
runners_data.note: Hold-up type with mixed recent form, neither turf run this summer suggests improvement
runners_data.comment: 0-14 and hard to enthuse over after latest 10l defeat here when behind two of these
runners_data.spotlight: 0-15 but the odd promising effort, including a close second at Newcastle in March (7f); neither of his turf runs this summer suggest he is the answer today.

races.paceDynamic: No Nay Nevermind stands alone as the only confirmed front-runner, which creates a crucial tactical advantage in this 6f sprint. With eight hold-up horses behind her including Zu Run, Mister Sky Blue, and Endowed, she can dictate terms without early pressure and save energy for the finish. The lack of pace pressure means the race will develop into a sprint from 2f out when the hold-up brigade make their moves. This race shape strongly favours horses with early pace or those that can sit close to the leader, as the wall of hold-up horses will struggle to get into contention from too far back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Wins
scenarios.trigger: If No Nay Nevermind gets an easy lead without early pressure from the field.
scenarios.body: She can control the fractions and kick clear when the hold-up horses are still getting organized behind her. The lack of early pace allows her to save energy and prove too strong in the final furlong despite her poor recent form.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Early Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If one of the hold-up horses sits closer than usual to track No Nay Nevermind.
scenarios.body: Zu Run or Endowed could position themselves handier than their usual style suggests and benefit from the soft pace before pouncing. Their class advantage over the pace-setter becomes decisive in the final 100 yards.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Succeeds
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and the field compacts turning for home.
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get a perfect setup to unleash their finishing kicks simultaneously. Mister Sky Blue's course form or Summerstorms Dream's improved headgear could prove decisive in a blanket finish.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapses Completely
scenarios.trigger: If No Nay Nevermind stops quickly after setting uncontested fractions.
scenarios.body: The race becomes a complete lottery as nine horses converge in the final furlong with no clear pace setup. Any of the hold-up horses could benefit from the chaos, with jockey strength becoming crucial.

watchPoints.text: No Nay Nevermind's early positioning - if she misses the break or gets pressured early, the entire pace scenario changes
Zu Run and Endowed tracking closer than usual given the lack of pace - their positioning in the first furlong is crucial
Summerstorms Dream's start - her recurring slow starts could prove fatal in a race with limited pace
Any horse showing early pace to challenge No Nay Nevermind - would completely alter the tactical picture
The field's positioning at halfway - if they're all still in a bunch, expect a cavalry charge finish

races.name: Hamilton Park EBF Maiden Stakes (Hamilton Park 2YO Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Casino Star
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £100,000 yearling; third foal from a Listed-placed 5f 2yo and 7f winner; half-brother to the 5f 2yo winner Bacor (RPR 75); top trainer is running at a 27% strike-rate with juveniles this year (20% over the past five years); high on the shortlist.

runners_data.name: Royal Heritage
runners_data.spotlight: 98,000gns yearling, 800,000euros breeze-up 2yo; seventh foal from unraced half-sister to US 1m Grade 3 winner Farhaan; closely related to 7f-1m winner Lattam (RPR 102) and a half-brother to three winners; connections had a promising juvenile winner (Alta Regina) at Lingfield recently.

runners_data.name: Sea Palace
runners_data.spotlight: February foal; 92,000gns foal, 120,000gns yearling; ninth foal from a 5f 2yo winner (including Listed; RPR 105); half-brother to five winners, including Nigel Nott (5f-6f AW; 95); trainer seeking first juvenile winner (0-9) of the season.

runners_data.name: Desert Move
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; third foal from a 6f juvenile winner (RPR 92); half-brother to the 1m2f AW winner Sharp Move; joint trainers have had three juvenile winners (11% strike-rate) this year, including Crystal Queen (same ownership) in the Hilary Needler at Beverley; market informative.

runners_data.name: My Mate Fitz
runners_data.spotlight: March foal; £75,000 vendor yearling; first foal from US Graded stakes-placed 5.5f turf 2yo winner Invincible Gal (RPR 98); already gelded; trainer has made a flying start this term with his juveniles running at over a 30% strike-rate, National Stakes winner Where Love Lives the most notable.

races.name: Robert Graham Millar Memorial Maiden Stakes (GBB/GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Florida Dreams
runners_data.note: Eight-year-old hold-up performer returning from hurdles with tactical disadvantage against uncontested leader
runners_data.comment: Grade 2 bumper winner and useful over hurdles; interesting contender on this Flat debut
runners_data.spotlight: Grade 2 bumper winner in April 2023, who also won twice over hurdles (2m) for Nicky Richards; 22-1, lacked the pace to challenge when fifth of nine on Flat debut at Haydock (11.5f, soft; Yafreh about 1l ahead in fourth) three weeks ago; likely to be seen in a better light once handicapping.

runners_data.name: Glory Of The Seas
runners_data.note: Highest-rated runner but hold-up style poorly suited to likely uncontested pace scenario, 33-day break manageable
runners_data.spotlight: 550,000gns yearling; steady improvement; beaten just over 7l (fourth) by the exciting Water To Wine on seasonal reappearance at Newbury (1m3f, good), before finishing third in a hot maiden at Chester's May Festival (12.5f maiden); gelded since and this looks the perfect opportunity to strike.

runners_data.name: Yafreh
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who could apply early pressure but recent form suggests limited winning ability
runners_data.comment: No threat on debut but attractive pedigree suggests he could have lots more to offer
runners_data.spotlight: Brother to 7f-1m2f winner Al Mubhir (RPR 115); showed similar level of ability in his two starts, last time 6-1 when a rallying fourth at Haydock (11.5f, soft; Florida Dreams fifth) three weeks ago; slightly more required and he will soon be handicapping.

runners_data.name: Aussie Pearl
runners_data.note: Sole front runner returning from 231-day break but perfectly positioned tactically if retaining fitness
runners_data.spotlight: In the mix on Leicester debut (1m maiden fillies; 7-2) last October but soundly beaten by a long odds-on favourite at Newmarket (1m2f, good) a fortnight later; off since and, even receiving the fillies' allowance, this looks a tough race in which to reappear; stamina to prove.

runners_data.name: Togeather Forever
runners_data.note: Weak form and hold-up style make him unsuited to likely race shape
runners_data.comment: Half-brother to four winners (three useful) but probably a longer-term prospect
runners_data.spotlight: Half-brother to four winners, including the Listed scorer Ralston Road (1m2f-1m6f); slowly into stride and always behind on debut here (1m1f novice; hooded, 40-1) a fortnight ago; this longer trip should suit but time will be his ultimate friend; highly unlikely candidate.

races.paceDynamic: Aussie Pearl is the sole confirmed front runner and will face no early pressure in a field lacking pace angles. This creates a sustainable tempo with Yafreh likely tracking as the only prominent runner, while Glory Of The Seas, Florida Dreams and Togeather Forever all prefer to be held up. The uncontested lead scenario strongly favours front running tactics, giving Aussie Pearl a significant positional advantage over the hold-up brigade who will need the pace to collapse.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Uncontested Leader Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Aussie Pearl secures an easy lead without pressure from Yafreh early
scenarios.body: She can dictate fractions and has enough in hand to resist late challenges from the hold-up horses who face a stiff task giving her a head start. The 231-day break becomes less relevant when she controls the race from the front.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Class Tells Late
scenarios.trigger: If Glory Of The Seas can overcome the tactical disadvantage with superior ability
scenarios.body: His OR 87 rating is significantly higher than rivals and the Varian stable often brings horses to peak fitness after breaks. The hold-up style works if Aussie Pearl sets unsustainable fractions under pressure.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If Yafreh can apply early pressure to Aussie Pearl and outstay her
scenarios.body: The Fahey-trained gelding has shown consistent form levels and his prominent style could exploit any fitness doubts about the long-absent leader. His recent Haydock fourth suggests he's in good heart.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Fitness Concerns Surface
scenarios.trigger: If Aussie Pearl's 231-day absence tells in the closing stages
scenarios.body: The two-year-old filly may not have the stamina reserves to complete the job, allowing the more race-fit hold-up horses to pick up the pieces. Florida Dreams could benefit from his recent runs despite moderate form.

watchPoints.text: Aussie Pearl shows any signs of rustiness early given her 231-day absence could undermine the tactical advantage
Yafreh applies more pressure than expected to the leader which could change the race complexion significantly
Glory Of The Seas gets a strong early position despite his hold-up rating as this would improve his chances considerably
The early pace development between Aussie Pearl and Yafreh shapes the entire contest for the hold-up horses

races.name: Every Race Live On RacingTV Handicap

runners_data.name: Hi Lord
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who won here when headgear was removed, making him the main pace threat alongside Canaria Queen
runners_data.comment: Headgear removed and doubled his tally with a narrow win over C&D a month ago
runners_data.spotlight: Headgear removed when he pounced late to beat Mount Ruapehu over C&D (good; from 3lb lower) on penultimate start; ran to an identical level on RPRs when third here last week; should give his running at a track (form figures 2613) which suits.

runners_data.name: Canaria Queen
runners_data.note: In-form prominent mare with excellent 5f record who should press Hi Lord for the early lead
runners_data.comment: No match for stablemate Marajito over C&D (good, 9-2) last week; remains in fine fettle.
runners_data.spotlight: In-form mare; twice successful this season, including at Musselburgh (5f, Class 6, good; from 5lb lower); runner-up at Ripon on last two outings (Tees Aggregates a close third on penultimate start); has no issues with this track; merits respect.

runners_data.name: South Parade
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse running 8lb lower than last win but has struggled this season and reared at the start last time
runners_data.comment: On a dangerous mark but she doesn't look in much form
runners_data.spotlight: 8lb lower than when last successful at Thirsk (5f Class 4, good to firm; 6-4 favourite) last August; struggled this season and reared at the start when in rear throughout (behind two of these) at Ripon latest.

runners_data.name: Tees Aggregates
runners_data.note: Hold-up runner who stayed on well for third at Ripon last time and has shown his best form over this 5f trip
runners_data.comment: Recent efforts respectable and has a good 0-70 record; enters calculations
runners_data.spotlight: Didn't have things go smoothly but stuck on positively down the outer when closing third (Canaria Queen second) at Ripon (5f, good) a fortnight ago; two of his three wins have been at tracks with a stiff uphill finish (Beverley and Leicester) and he's handicapped to go close at the least.

runners_data.name: Pal Joey
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse wearing a visor who won over 5f on the all-weather but has been less effective since returning to turf
runners_data.spotlight: Won at Newcastle (AW; from a similar mark) in January on his first attempt over 5f; less effective since, dwelling and failing to make his presence felt over C&D (tenth of 13; Class 3) latest; this race is easier and Paul Mulrennan is back aboard.

runners_data.name: Highland Bear
runners_data.note: Hold-up maiden making handicap debut after 46 days off, looking a work in progress
runners_data.comment: Showed promise in all three qualifying races; makes handicap/turf debut in low-grade race
runners_data.spotlight: Signs of ability in AW novice/maidens (5f-6f) but has looked something of a work in progress; taken out of her intended handicap debut at Wetherby (5.5f, good to firm) last week because of unsuitable ground, so this projected softer surface could suit; best watched for the moment.

runners_data.name: Mount Ruapehu
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse who was beaten by Hi Lord over course and distance and struggled at longer trips since
runners_data.comment: Three 6f wins on AW this year; narrow 5f turf defeat this month; shade flat latest
runners_data.spotlight: Justified favouritism at Southwell (6f) in April and pipped by Hi Lord over C&D (good) the following week; less competitive at Catterick (7f) and Carlisle (6f) on last two outings and the handicapper might have his measure.

races.paceDynamic: Hi Lord and Canaria Queen will contest the early lead in this small field, with both having prominent tendencies and recent 5f experience at this track. Their likely pace battle should create a solid gallop that will stretch the field early over this sharp 5f trip. The four hold-up horses (South Parade, Tees Aggregates, Pal Joey, Mount Ruapehu) will need the front two to go hard enough to come back to them in the final furlong. This race shape clearly favours the prominent runners who can sit close to the pace without getting embroiled in a speed duel.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Dual Pace Collapse
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Lord and Canaria Queen engage in a sustained speed battle from the gates
scenarios.body: Both prominent runners will weaken in the final furlong after setting unsustainable fractions. This creates the perfect setup for the hold-up horses to sweep past tired leaders in the closing stages.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Canaria Queen Dominates
scenarios.trigger: If Canaria Queen can steal a march on Hi Lord and control the tempo
scenarios.body: Her superior recent form and tactical speed will allow her to dictate terms and kick clear when it matters. The in-form mare's two recent seconds show she's primed to return to winning ways.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hi Lord Stays Strong
scenarios.trigger: If Hi Lord can secure an uncontested lead with Canaria Queen settling behind
scenarios.body: He'll repeat his course and distance success by maintaining a sustainable pace before quickening. His recent headgear removal suggests connections have found the key to unlocking his best form.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late Closer Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If the prominent pair set steady fractions that don't sufficiently test the field
scenarios.body: One of the hold-up horses will have enough left to mount a telling late challenge. Tees Aggregates showed improved form last time and could benefit most from this tactical scenario.

watchPoints.text: Hi Lord and Canaria Queen must be monitored for how quickly they establish positions, as both will want to press forward early
South Parade has shown starting issues recently including rearing, which could compromise his chances from the off
Pal Joey's dwelling tendencies could leave him with too much ground to make up over this sharp 5f trip
Highland Bear is making her handicap debut off a long break and may need the experience
The pace battle between the two prominent runners will determine whether hold-up horses get their optimal race shape

races.name: Indigo Unified Comms Handicap

runners_data.name: No Return
runners_data.note: Prominent runner who should get ideal position tracking Iris Dancer; trainer Johnston has modest recent record
runners_data.comment: Ex-Irish gelding who's proved inconsistent for this yard having missed six months
runners_data.spotlight: A fair 6f scorer in Ireland last spring for Daniel Murphy; made a promising start for current yard with second at Lingfield (6f) in January but he's failed to build on it, a below-par fourth of seven back at Lingfield (6f) last time.

runners_data.name: Ingleby Archie
runners_data.note: Prominent style suits the pace setup; apprentice Nicholls takes 5lb claim but trainer struggling for winners
runners_data.comment: Fourth on seasonal reappearance at Wetherby (5.5f; 15-8 fav); now sits 2lb lower; chance.
runners_data.spotlight: Scored twice (5f/6f) last May and took a step forward with third of seven in 6f Catterick handicap 20 days ago; not out of things from an easing mark.

runners_data.name: Pop Star
runners_data.note: Hold-up horse hampered last time; tongue-strap reapplied after recent Carlisle success only 2 days ago
runners_data.comment: Scored over 5f at Carlisle ten days ago; recorded a 6f win off current mark two years ago
runners_data.spotlight: Capitalised on a reduced mark when readily defeating a next-time-out winner in ten-runner handicap at Carlisle (5f) in refitted tongue-strap 12 days ago; hampered when favourite there on Monday; seriously considered.

runners_data.name: Novak
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer but faces traffic concerns with most of field racing similarly
runners_data.comment: 7f runner-up at Ayr recently; return to 6f isn't an obvious plus but it's a stiff finish
runners_data.spotlight: On the go since the turn of the year but largely in good nick and he came second of nine in 7f Ayr handicap three weeks ago; must enter calculations off the same mark.

runners_data.name: Jet Warrior
runners_data.note: Low-mileage improver whose hold-up style may struggle against prominent racers in small field
runners_data.comment: Has won his last two races; 10lb rise; a contender, although this softer ground a concern
runners_data.spotlight: Low-mileage 4yo who has thrived since sent handicapping, landing 6f handicaps at Ayr (good to firm) and Ripon (good) last month; another good run when third at Carlisle (6f, good to soft) last night; not taken at all lightly.

runners_data.name: Iris Dancer
runners_data.note: Lone front runner and course specialist; bounced back to form at this track and won this race last year
runners_data.comment: Her form has been mixed this season but she's a well handicapped course specialist
runners_data.spotlight: Course specialist; only sixth of nine on her first run of 2026 here over C&D six days ago but she took this prize 12 months ago, so no surprise if she bounces back; usually wears headgear but it is now removed.

runners_data.name: Impressor
runners_data.note: Veteran hold-up horse with course form; 9-year-old needs things to fall right but recent third here was encouraging
runners_data.comment: Underwhelming since promising reappearance run but he has a strong record at Hamilton
runners_data.spotlight: A three-time winner (including over C&D) here who got back on track when third of nine over C&D six days ago; goes well on soft ground, so this veteran is in the mix, especially if the rain comes.

races.paceDynamic: Iris Dancer will take the field along from the front with only No Return and Ingleby Archie likely to track her early. The pace should be genuine but not frantic over this 6f trip, as Iris Dancer has proven she can sustain her effort at Hamilton. With most of the field comprising hold-up horses (Pop Star, Novak, Jet Warrior, Impressor), there will be plenty of runners coming from off the pace in the final two furlongs. This race shape clearly favours the prominent racers and early pace-setters who can avoid the inevitable traffic problems that will engulf the large group of hold-up horses.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Front Running Dominance
scenarios.trigger: If Iris Dancer gets an uncontested lead and the pace is steady
scenarios.body: Her course specialisation and tactical advantage allow her to kick clear in the final furlong while the hold-up horses struggle to make up ground. The lack of early pace pressure means she retains enough stamina to see off late challengers.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Horse Prevails
scenarios.trigger: If No Return or Ingleby Archie track Iris Dancer closely and strike at the right moment
scenarios.body: These horses get the perfect trip tracking the leader before moving smoothly into contention, avoiding the scrimmaging behind. Their prominent racing style allows them to quicken clear while the hold-up brigade gets caught in traffic.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Late Surge Success
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes too strong early or Iris Dancer fades quickly
scenarios.body: The hold-up horses get a perfect setup with a strong gallop and collapsing leaders. Jet Warrior and Pop Star, both in good form, can unleash their finishing kicks to maximum effect.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Veteran Experience Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Impressor gets the ideal soft ground conditions and perfect positioning
scenarios.body: The 9-year-old's course experience and ground preference allows him to navigate through traffic expertly. His proven Hamilton record and recent course form gives him the edge over less experienced rivals.

watchPoints.text: Iris Dancer getting a soft lead could prove decisive given her course specialisation and last year's win in this race
Pop Star running just 2 days after last victory at Carlisle may show signs of a quick turnaround
No Return and Ingleby Archie's ability to track Iris Dancer early will determine if the front runner gets an easy time
The large group of hold-up horses (Pop Star, Novak, Jet Warrior, Impressor) creating potential traffic problems in the straight
Jet Warrior's recent handicap wins suggest continued improvement but hold-up style works against him here

races.name: Hampton By Hilton Hamilton Park Handicap

runners_data.name: Mwafaq
runners_data.note: Hold up horse who needs strong pace to be effective, recent hat-trick winner but may struggle if Spirit Catcher sets modest fractions
runners_data.comment: Chance was compromised at Southwell by a wide trip; remains of interest
runners_data.spotlight: Won reappearance, completing the hat-trick, at Thirsk (7f, good; from 4lb lower) in April; pressed the winner hard at Ayr (1m, good to firm) three weeks ago; this is a slightly longer trip; useful claimer in the saddle.

runners_data.name: The Sweet Escape
runners_data.note: Prominent racer perfectly positioned to track Spirit Catcher, recent Nottingham winner shows she handles similar tactical scenarios
runners_data.comment: C&D win last month; went close at Leicester on penultimate start; needs more in this grade
runners_data.spotlight: Took advantage of a drop back in trip and ease in grade (into a Class 6) when scrambling home at Nottingham (8.5f, good; from 3lb lower) in April; beaten by a nose off this mark at Leicester (1m) in May and consistent since; possible.

runners_data.name: Pisanello
runners_data.note: Dual course winner dropped significantly in weights, hold up style needs genuine gallop to be effective from his wide draw
runners_data.comment: 9yo who is nothing like the force of old but his Hamilton fourth wasn't devoid of promise
runners_data.spotlight: Dual C&D winner; failed to score since York (1m1f, Class 4) two years ago; way down the weights now and 4l fourth to Perfidia over C&D (now 4lb lower and claimer ridden) on penultimate start, but usual tale of modest late headway continued at Carlisle last time; patience with him is wearing thin.

runners_data.name: Condotti
runners_data.note: Prominent runner seeking first career win, 10lb lower than last placed effort suggests handicapper has found his level
runners_data.comment: Ten-race maiden but he ran some good races last season and reappears on a career-low mark
runners_data.spotlight: Still seeking first win (0-11) and now 10lb lower than when runner-up at Ffos Las (1m, good; 2-1 favourite) last August; weakened quickly when last of nine on reappearance at Carlisle (1m1f, good) 12 days ago.

runners_data.name: Hunterian
runners_data.note: Improved on turf debut at Redcar showing early speed, inexperienced at this trip but well drawn to track the pace
runners_data.comment: Unexposed; makes turf debut down in trip after four runs on AW; has a bit to prove
runners_data.spotlight: Well beaten in four AW starts (at around a mile); took a slight step forward, showing speed, when third on turf debut at Redcar (7f, good to firm; 12-1) a fortnight ago; opposition suitable, but this return to 8.5f may not help; low mileage.

runners_data.name: Perfidia
runners_data.note: Course winner with strong finishing kick, needs more pace than Spirit Catcher likely to provide but proven here
runners_data.comment: He's been in good form since returning to action and could be in the shake-up
runners_data.spotlight: Did enough to justify favouritism over C&D (good; from 2lb lower; Pisanello fourth) three back; held form reasonably well since, failing to get the breaks at Ripon (1m, good; fifth) last week; Jake Dickson's 7lb claim continues to be handy.

runners_data.name: Spirit Catcher
runners_data.note: Natural front runner with recent winning form over similar trip, perfectly positioned to control the race tempo
runners_data.comment: Arrives in form, winning over 1m1f here before a good 2nd at Ripon; new trip; key player
runners_data.spotlight: Returned to winning ways at Musselburgh (1m1f, good; from 4lb lower) in April and runner-up twice since, stamina seemingly overstretched behind the thriving Alpine Sierra at Musselburgh (12.5f) latest; enters calculations back over a more suitable 8.5f.

runners_data.name: Motawaared
runners_data.note: Hold up horse who has been slowly away recently, needs to overcome poor gate manners to be competitive
runners_data.comment: Did not get seriously competitive when seventh on first two starts this season (1m4f/1m1f)
runners_data.spotlight: Placed in a novice and a maiden (both 1m) for George Boughey; low key (0-4, often slowly away) since joining Jim Goldie for 12,000gns; drops into a Class 6 for the first time, though, with cheekpieces added; no forlorn hope.

runners_data.name: South Road
runners_data.note: Shock Ayr winner returning from break, hold up style poorly suited to likely steady tempo
runners_data.comment: 40-1 winner of a 6f handicap here last summer; there are stamina doubts over this far
runners_data.spotlight: Shock 6f winner at Ayr (good to soft; 40-1, from 5lb higher) last July; not much to enthuse about since (0-5) but she was returning from a two-month break when fifth at Ayr (1m, good to firm; Mwafaq runner-up) latest; stamina is a major risk over 8.5f.

runners_data.name: Tees George
runners_data.note: Recent Beverley winner with proven finishing speed, needs to overcome 29-day break and poor recent Beverley form
runners_data.spotlight: Fourth of 22 at Doncaster (1m, good to soft) in March and built on that when winning at Beverley (8.5f) the following month; latest Beverley effort was not so good and he has fared no better than sixth in six races from a mark of 61 and higher.

runners_data.name: Millbuie
runners_data.note: Long-term maiden whose hold up style requires stronger pace than this race will provide
runners_data.comment: Yet to win but he comes here on the back of a solid Ayr sixth; more is still needed
runners_data.spotlight: 25-race maiden; had run of the race at Newcastle (1m2f; third, 16-1) last week but was unable to make it count; no reason to think that this return to turf can unlock the door; others are more convincing.

races.paceDynamic: Spirit Catcher will lead from the front with minimal pressure, as only The Sweet Escape and Condotti are likely to race prominently early. This creates a sustainable gallop that will suit horses positioned closer to the pace rather than those held up at the back. The lack of early speed means Spirit Catcher can dictate terms through steady sectionals before quickening. This race shape strongly favours prominent racers and front runners who can position themselves within striking distance of Spirit Catcher's controlled tempo.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Running Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Spirit Catcher maintains an uncontested lead through steady fractions
scenarios.body: Spirit Catcher can dictate ideal fractions and kick clear in the straight without having expended energy in early pace battles. His recent Musselburgh win shows he thrives when controlling the tempo over similar trips.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Tracker Strikes
scenarios.trigger: If The Sweet Escape or Condotti can track Spirit Catcher and outkick him late
scenarios.body: The prominent runners get the perfect tow behind the leader and can use superior finishing speed when Spirit Catcher's stamina wavers. The moderate early pace sets up a sprint finish that suits horses with tactical speed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold Up Horse Times Run
scenarios.trigger: If the pace becomes genuinely slow and holds up horses get cover before unleashing late
scenarios.body: Mwafaq and Perfidia can use their proven finishing kicks to sweep past tiring leaders in a truly-run finale. Both have shown strong closing sectionals when getting the right race setup.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Surprise Improver Emerges
scenarios.trigger: If the favorites falter and an outsider benefits from the tactical setup
scenarios.body: The steady tempo allows a horse like Pisanello or Tees George to stay closer than usual and capitalize on their lightweight advantages. The race shape could expose stamina doubts in some better-rated rivals.

watchPoints.text: Spirit Catcher breaks slowly or fails to lead as his front running style is crucial to the race setup
The Sweet Escape settles too close to Spirit Catcher early and compromises both horses' chances
Mwafaq and Perfidia struggle to get into contention if Spirit Catcher sets pedestrian fractions
Hunterian shows inexperience at the trip and fails to stay the extended distance on just his second turf start
Track the early positioning of Condotti as his prominent style could benefit most if Spirit Catcher sets controlled tempo
